before.lead: A borrower should not have to try the wrong channel before learning how an item can be renewed. I help Briscoe County institutions organize public instructions around the material and the action needed.
before.decisionTitle: Put the right renewal channel beside each material.
before.decision: Caprock Public Library’s service page allows book renewals online but directs DVD renewals to telephone or in-person contact. It also says an item cannot be renewed when another borrower is waiting. For a library website, I would connect each material’s loan information to the appropriate renewal route and a clear staff-help option. A proposed check would follow a reader with both a book and a DVD: the page should make the different channels visible without implying that the same catalog action handles both. The library decides whether the particular item can renew. Public instructions can explain that boundary without asking the reader to disclose account details in a general website inquiry.

before.lead: Access to a digital resource is not the same as permission to share it with a class or club. I help Hartley County organizations explain who a resource is for, whether it is available locally and how to ask for help.
before.decisionTitle: Show the permitted use before the resource link.
before.decision: Channing School/Public Library's digital-resource page separates free resources, consortium resources and subscriptions whose local availability must be checked. Its Harrington Library Consortium notice says individual cardholders must not extend their access to schools, classes, clubs or other groups. For a proposed library website, I would keep audience, local availability and sign-in instructions together. A hypothetical club organizer with a personal library card should find the group-use question before sharing credentials. The aim is a useful public resource directory, with a clear staff route for uncertainty; the page should not infer a license or permission from a successful login.

scopes.title: Improve the existing resource directory
scopes.request: Select a resource and check its audience and access requirements before opening it.
scopes.supplies: The current resource list, approved licensing notices, local subscriptions and correct provider destinations.
scopes.check: A teacher or club organizer can see that an individual card's access does not establish group permission.

scopes.title: Build a library research and learning gateway
scopes.request: Find a suitable resource for the intended use and ask the responsible team when the published conditions do not settle it.
scopes.supplies: Approved resource descriptions, age or audience groupings, local availability, help contacts and review responsibilities.
scopes.check: A listed optional subscription is not presented as available at Channing until the library confirms it; free resources remain easy to find.

before.scopeTrigger: A focused update can improve labels and links around the current directory. A fuller build can reorganize learning and research tasks across resource providers. The library and providers define licensing and availability. Authentication, subscription management and account permissions are separate technical work; the public directory does not need to collect credentials.

before.lead: A borrower’s card privileges do not necessarily determine where an item can be returned. I help Moore County organizations explain the item, account category and originating location as separate parts of a lending service.
before.decisionTitle: Keep the originating branch attached to the return instruction.
before.decision: Moore County Libraries publishes different checkout limits for card categories, different material rules and a requirement to return an item to the same location where it was borrowed. Its policy also says DVDs and Blu-rays cannot be renewed. For a proposed library website, I would keep those decisions distinct. Imagine a borrower with an established card who borrowed a DVD from one branch and is now closer to another. The card category does not erase the published return-location rule, and an online account link does not promise renewal for that material. Clear content can help the borrower find the correct branch and ask staff about a problem. It should not infer borrowing eligibility or calculate penalties from a general policy summary.

scopes.supplies: Approved lending categories, material rules, branch details and consistent links to the existing system.
scopes.check: A DVD borrower reaches the published return guidance without a generic renew button being explained as a guaranteed extension.

before.lead: A household account restriction can be explained without publishing another person’s borrowing. I help Gray County businesses turn that kind of customer decision into clear website content.
before.decisionTitle: Explain a shared account restriction without exposing another person’s borrowing.
before.decision: Lovett Memorial Library groups patrons by household and says a fine on one grouped card restricts the group’s services. Its confidentiality policy distinguishes the amount needed to settle a charge from authors, titles or subjects, which are not discussed without presentation of the borrower’s card. It also says Pampa cannot accept payment for another library’s fines. For a proposed account-help page, I would explain the shared consequence and the appropriate private next step without asking a household member to publish someone else’s borrowing history. The public page can identify that a restriction may concern a grouped account and direct the visitor to staff. It should preserve the distinction between learning how to resolve an amount and receiving details about the underlying materials. If the obligation belongs to another library, the instructions need the correct receiving institution rather than a generic pay-here message.

before.lead: A piano owner may need information to make a buying or selling decision before asking for maintenance. I help Dauphin County specialists explain the purpose of an appraisal alongside their tuning and repair work.
before.decisionTitle: Ask what decision the piano appraisal needs to support.
before.decision: Scott D. Portzline Piano Services advertises Harrisburg-area service and describes appraisals of a piano’s condition and value for several purposes, alongside tuning, repairs and moving. For a piano-service website, I can clarify that assessment offer or build a fuller introduction distinguishing the questions each service answers. Someone considering a piano purchase should be able to explain the decision and request an assessment without being routed straight into a routine tuning appointment.

scopes.supplies: Accurate service descriptions, actual appraisal outputs and how further services are agreed.

decisions.label: Identify the decision and instrument
decisions.body: Invite the purpose of the assessment and enough detail to identify the particular piano. Explain the accepted appraisal purposes rather than treating every inquiry as a general pricing question or routine maintenance appointment.

decisions.label: Prepare useful context
decisions.body: Ask for known history, observed concerns and access arrangements through approved prompts. The customer should describe what they know without diagnosing the instrument or selecting technical work before assessment.

decisions.label: Explain the output and later services
decisions.body: State what the appraisal actually supplies and any applicable limits. Let the customer ask about later tuning, repairs or moving while making clear those services need their own agreement. Do not imply another party automatically accepts the assessment.
